text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING emma — Canary cluster 'dedicated-eu-1' after roll v2.3.4 shows 95th latency spike ~3x and sustained throughput drop 40% since 12:03 UTC. Kernel fallback logs present. Auto-rollout paused.

emma: on it. joining the call now. can someone paste which hosts are affected?

raj: affected hosts list: ded-eu1-rt-0[5-8], ded-eu1-rt-1[0-2]. seeing repeated kernel fallback entries in /var/log/runtime.log around the deploy window.

sophie: paging timeline: deploy started 12:00, canary at 12:01 moved 10% traffic, 12:03 alert fires.

emma: ok. first triage — is this the batching change from the release? liam?

liam: yes — v2.3.4 turned on 'adaptive_continuous_batching_v2' by default for canary. also enabled aggressive KV-prefix caching eviction heuristics. rollout policy was staged but canary got the flag.

carlos: we've got 3 customer reports of timeout errors affecting embeddings requests (support tickets 5421, 5422, 5423). low volume but high priority customers. they see long tail latencies >8s.

emma: thanks. raj, can you drop a snippet of the kernel fallback log?

raj: here's a tail:

```
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z runtime[pid=4821]: kernel_fallback: selected slow-path kernel for attention because quantized kernel failed verification
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z runtime[pid=4821]: kv_cache_miss=0.38 batch_size=16 queue_wait_ms=120 schedule_delay_ms=22
2026-03-15T12:03:13Z runtime[pid=4821]: kernel_fallback: increasing per-token latency by 220ms
```

emma: queue_wait_ms=120 on canary is bad. normally <10. sounds like backpressure in scheduling combined with kernel fallback causing cascading latency.

sophie: observed token-level latency heatmap — spikes align with fallback windows. batch size fluctuating higher than intended (16-32) during the spike. not stable.

emma: mitigation options: 1) flip kill-switch to disable adaptive_continuous_batching_v2 for canary 2) rollback canary to previous revision 3) temporarily route traffic off canary to other regions. prefer least invasive first.

liam: we can flip kill-switch in config service quickly: `./configctl set /features/adaptive_continuous_batching_v2 false --env canary` Should act within ~30s. rollback requires deploy pipeline and ~5-10m.

emma: do kill-switch. raj, sophie watch metrics. carlos please ping affected customers that we're mitigating and will follow up.

liam: executing kill-switch now.

deploy-bot: config write accepted. change propagated to canary at 12:07:02 UTC.

emma: monitoring...

raj: initial telemetry: queue_wait_ms drops from ~120ms -> ~15ms across canary hosts within one minute. kernel_fallback logs stop appearing.

sophie: 95th latency trending down from 3.2s -> 0.9s in the next 3 minutes. throughput climbing back toward expected.

carlos: sent update to customers: "We observed an increase in request latency tied to a canary feature. We've disabled the feature and are seeing improvements. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

emma: nice. mark as mitigated for customer impact. we should still investigate root cause: why did the batching heuristic increase batch sizes and trigger fallback? raj can you grab runtime traces and kernel verification failure details.

raj: copying logs to /tmp/canary-investigation.tar.gz and starting a deeper trace now. early signal shows that quantized-kernel verification occasionally fails when batch size crosses threshold X due to alignment on last dimension — hitting slow-path. combined with adaptive batching expanding batch size under low-latency SLO pressure, it pushed many requests into that slow path.

emma: that matches. followup actions: - (A) postmortem ticket and RCA - (B) revert change in main branch and re-run verification tests for quant kernels across batch size sweep - (C) add a safety cap to batching algorithm for canary stage - (D) update runbook to prefer kill-switch before full rollback for similar symptoms

liam: I'll open release rollback PR once we confirm patch; target revert commit r=immediate if tests fail.

sophie: also recommending an alert tweak: add a correlation alert when kernel_fallback rate > 1% AND avg_batch_size > 12. will file infra alert.

emma: handoff — my shift ends in 30m. raj, sophie you'll take on-call for next 6h. liam handle release patch. carlos keep customer comms and collect exact request IDs from tickets.

emma: closing paging loop: :white_check_mark: mitigation applied (feature flag disabled). will keep thread open for RCA notes and next steps. if anything regresses, escalate.

raj: confirming traces uploaded, starting bisect on batching heuristic.

liam: creating revert PR and CI matrix run. ETA 2h.

carlos: logged follow-up meetings with customers, they want a timeline but appreciate the quick mitigation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT update — Status=mitigated, Severity=SEV3, started=12:03 UTC, mitigated=12:07 UTC, assigned=[emma, raj, sophie], channels=#incidents,#eng-runtime,#support

sophie: adding an item to postmortem: test quant-kernel across edge batch sizes and gating rollout by that test.

emma: thanks team. signing off from active page — will catch up on the RCA doc later.

raj: ack. taking lead.

liam: ack.

carlos: ack, closing customer comms loop later today.

(reacts: :eyes: by raj, :thumbsup: by liam, :sparkles: by carlos)
